doc.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025

title: Arranging workshops and the cringe moment
summary: Alan Broadbent's cringe moment is the joy moment too; Mays recalls the BMI Writers Workshop with Brookmeyer and Albam.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: There’s a lot to be said for that, develop your own style. I think the things you learn to do and not to do really make a strong impression on you when you’re trying it on your own. Your friend and sometimes bandmate Alan Broadbent described that when you bring in an arrangement and you hear it for the first time, he called it the “cringe moment.”

Also the joy moment. It’s so great to – especially if you’re working with a big band or orchestra like Alan does a lot and I do from time to time. It’s such a joy to hear it with live instruments. Now we can mock it up on synthesizers and before, in the old days, we couldn’t. We just played and heard it on the piano. But it’s the cringe moment but also joyous when it all comes together and it works. And you know it’s great, we had workshops back in the day, I remember I was a member of the BMI Writers Workshop in New York with Bob Brookmeyer and Manny Albam. And we’d bring things in and try them. And you know they worked or they didn’t, and we talked about why they didn’t and fixed it. And it’s, yeah.
